rationale: The chief priests and scribes introduce this citation with their own words, "for this is what the prophet has written" (40.2.5), and quote directly, which is why the type is quotation rather than allusion. The label is explicit because of the citation formula, not because the wording matches Micah exactly: checked directly against both passages as shipped in this app, Matthew 2:6 drops Micah 5:2's "Ephrathah" and its closing clause ("One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity"), reverses "small" to "by no means least," and imports "shepherd" from Micah 5:4 rather than 5:2 -- so toRange spans 5:2-4 to cover the verse the shepherd clause is actually drawn from. The speaker is the chief priests and scribes within the narrative, not Matthew's own fulfillment-formula voice used elsewhere in this chapter (2:15, 17, 23).
